tests.stimulus: rst=0 is held across 4 rising edges and then released on a falling edge, with reset repeated once every 950 cycles; nine complete Top instances respectively run isa_0.mem, isa_1.mem, isa_2.mem, isa_3.mem, isa_shifts.mem, isa_boundaries.mem, and isa_persistence.mem supplied with the submission, as well as the publicly provided default program.mem and the built-in image with PROGRAM_FILE empty. The software consists of known 16-bit hexadecimal instructions; unloaded ROM words are NOP. Actual instruction fetching wraps from 1023 to 0; RAM addresses 0, 0x3fd, and the 0x7fd alias are written before being read. In its first round, the persistence software writes 0x13579bdf into RAM[321]; after subsequent resets, input 0 selects reading followed by output without rewriting, checking RAM retention across reset. No deterministic expectations are established for addresses that have never been written.
tests.expected: clk advances on the rising edge; rst is an active-low synchronous reset. One active reset edge clears the fetch address, fetched instruction, execute token, writeback token, and eight general-purpose registers to zero; result_valid, result_data, and the peripheral read-hold state are cleared to zero. Data RAM is not initialized and is not cleared by reset; reads of addresses that have never been written are undefined. Legal deterministic data expectations require writing before reading. Instruction ROM is initialized to zero, then the words covered by PROGRAM_FILE are loaded; addresses are 10-bit word addresses and wrap modulo 1024. ROM does not change on reset. The file may use readmemh address markers; only known 16-bit data words constitute a legal program.
tests.checker: The independent, self-contained model/model.sv computes expected using only reset, stimulus, and input history, without reading DUT outputs. The monitor counts every rising edge of the input-source clock from the start of simulation, samples actual and expected 1ns after the edge, and the scoreboard performs a four-state comparison, reporting UVM_ERROR on a mismatch and saving the first error and total count. The input-source clock is clk; comparisons are skipped only for the first 2 rising edges at simulation startup. Thereafter, result_valid and result_data are always compared on every rising edge, including data holding when valid=0, active-low synchronous reset, and restart. Check the actual total sample count, the result transactions of each legal software program, and output activity; passing with zero comparisons is not allowed.

tests.stimulus: The program reads a 32-bit value that changes every cycle from 0x3fe, consecutively executes opcode1..10, and STOREs the results to 0x3ff; it includes R0 destinations, adjacent dependencies, two-level bypassing, 40 sets of different random logic combinations, and positive/negative/full-bit patterns.
tests.expected: Instruction bits [15:9] are the seven-bit arithmetic opcode; destination/source1/source2 are [8:6]/[5:3]/[2:0], respectively. opcode 0 is NOP; 1 ADD and 2 ADDF both compute source1+source2; 3 SUB and 4 SUBF both compute source1−source2; 5 AND, 6 OR, 7 XOR, 8 NAND, 9 NOR, and 10 NXOR perform the respective bitwise operations, with the last three inverting the corresponding results. All operations retain the low 32 bits, with no overflow exception and no separate flags register; F in the name adds no flag behavior. Unknown encodings act as operations with no data result, but are still subject to the default R0 writeback behavior.

tests.stimulus: The three shift opcodes opcode11/12/13 are each subjected to the full six-bit shift amounts 0..63, re-LOADing the operand from input MMIO each time and immediately STOREing the result. Inputs on falling edges include 0x13579bdf, 0, 32-bit random patterns, and a directed 0x80000000 tail segment, covering positive, negative, and zero values; no claim is made of exhaustive coverage of the Cartesian product of every shift amount with all operands. In addition, R3 is set up as 0x12000000 and then output after LOADC with low byte 0x34; the independent expected value is 0x12000034.
tests.expected: Seven-bit opcodes 11, 12, and 13 are logical right shift, arithmetic right shift, and left shift, respectively. They read and write the same register specified by [8:6]; the shift amount is the full unsigned value of [5:0], 0–63, and is not reduced modulo 31. Logical shifts beyond 31 bits yield zero; arithmetic right shifts sign-extend. The first five bits [15:11]=9 indicate LOADC, with destination [10:8]; concatenate the old high 24 bits of that register with the immediate [7:0], preserving the high bits rather than performing a sign-extended whole-word load.

tests.stimulus: The original four software programs STORE before LOAD at RAM addresses 512..515; the added software covers address 0, 0x3fd, and the aliasing of 32-bit register address 0x7fd to the low 10 bits 0x3fd, each time writing before reading and then immediately outputting. Chain LOAD dependencies and switch between RAM, input MMIO, and result MMIO reads; the irrelevant bits [7:3] in LOAD/STORE encodings are all 1, and accesses still use the low 10 bits of the address register.
tests.expected: The first five bits being 8 indicate LOAD, with destination [10:8] and address register [2:0]; the first five bits being 10 indicate STORE, with address register [10:8] and data register [2:0]. In both instructions, [7:3] do not participate in address calculation. The actual address is the low 10 bits of the corresponding 32-bit register, with no byte conversion. LOAD initiates a synchronous read on its execution edge; the data obtained after that edge is used for writeback and bypassing. STORE writes on the execution edge. Synchronous reads take priority over writes; when no read occurs, the read-hold state remains unchanged. RAM addresses are 0–0x3fd; 0x3fe and 0x3ff are peripherals and do not write RAM.

tests.stimulus: input_data changes on falling edges; synchronous sampling is observed through LOAD0x3fe followed by arithmetic and STORE0x3ff. First output once and read back 0x3ff, then actually STORE0x3fe, checking cycle by cycle that this write neither issues result_valid nor changes result_data. Then LOAD0x3ff again to output the original held value, interspersing RAM transactions, non-result writes, HALT, and repeated resets. Provide 0x13579bdf for the initial 64 cycles of the first round and 0 for the initial 64 cycles of subsequent reset rounds; use random values on other falling edges, and provide 0x80000000 at the end. Combinational pass-through of input_data to writeback is not allowed.
tests.expected: The edge executing a LOAD at address 0x3fe samples input_data; reading 0x3ff obtains the pre-edge result_data. Both peripherals and RAM use synchronous reads with holding; consecutive switches between the two read sources must use the newly sampled source, and must not allow input_data to pass combinationally through to writeback. When executing a STORE at address 0x3ff and not performing a read operation, result_valid is set to 1 for one cycle after that edge, and result_data registers the store data; on every subsequent edge that is not a result write, result_valid is set to 0, while result_data holds until the next result write or reset. Writing 0x3fe does not change the result and does not write RAM. input_data may change on every falling clock edge; the sampling time is determined by the actual LOAD execution edge.

tests.stimulus: The original four software programs use zero, positive values, and an all-ones negative value to exercise taken and not-taken absolute/relative branches for condition codes 0..3. The added software explicitly executes unconditional JMP and JMPR, with JMPR offsets at the six-bit signed upper bound +31 and lower bound -32; recognizable STORE instructions are placed on the flushed younger path, and target outputs 0x1357 and 0x2468 distinguish the actual destinations. The absolute target register value 0x7ff must be truncated to 0x3ff, after which instruction fetching naturally wraps around to 0; condition codes 4..7 are actually applied and do not branch. Execution-edge outputs and the absence of delay slots are checked using token scheduling based on independent input history.
tests.expected: The first four bits 8 indicate JMP, with the absolute address coming from register [2:0]; 9 indicates JMPR, with the relative offset being the signed six-bit number in [5:0]. The first four bits 10 indicate a conditional absolute jump, and 11 a conditional relative jump. Condition code [11:9]: 0 means the register value is negative, 1 means nonnegative, 2 means zero, and 3 means nonzero; other conditions do not jump. The tested register is [8:6], and the absolute target register is [2:0]. Comparisons use signed 32-bit values. The absolute target retains the low 10 bits; the relative target is the fetch address before the execution edge plus sign_extend(offset)−2, finally retaining the low 10 bits. There are no separate condition flags and no delay slots. A taken jump clears the two younger tokens; otherwise the pipeline advances normally.

tests.stimulus: Continuously apply LOAD with immediate use, ALU to ALU to STORE, LOADC to shift to LOADC, and instruction fetching after branches, updating an independent interpreter at every input sampling edge. LOADC and shift consecutively write the same R3, so that the register read by the subsequent LOADC matches both the execute and writeback destinations; different new and old values check execute bypass priority. The specific upper-bit preservation sequence finally outputs 0x12000034. Compare MMIO cycle by cycle rather than only comparing result order, including the first execution after reset, LOAD holding P/I and inserting a bubble, and branches clearing younger tokens.
tests.expected:
To specify MMIO cycles precisely, abstract the pipeline as fetch address P, fetched instruction I, execute token X, and writeback token W. At each edge, first compute the execution value, memory transaction, and jump from pre-edge X, obtain the writeback value from pre-edge W, and read the register operands of I. For each operand of a non-NOP instruction, if the execution destination matches, preferentially use the current execution value; otherwise, if the writeback destination matches, use the current writeback value; otherwise read the pre-edge register. The current execution value of LOAD is zero; NOP does not use bypassing.

Without a stall, the edge places ROM[P] into I, I and the operands above into X, and the opcode/destination/result of X into W, increments P by one, and writes pre-edge W into the registers. The LOAD execution edge holds P and I, inserts an all-zero bubble into X, and still passes LOAD into W normally; thus, on the next edge, I uses LOAD writeback bypassing. A taken branch sets the new P to the target and clears I/X to zero, while W still receives the branch. Reset takes priority over these changes. MMIO is sampled or issued on the execution edge of X and must not be delayed until the register writeback edge. After reset, the first instruction ROM[0] enters I on the first edge with reset released, enters X on the second edge, and executes on the third edge.

tests.stimulus: The programs each write R0 and immediately consume it with an ALU instruction, exposing the result through STORE; use R0 again after inserting NOP/STORE/branches. The independent mirror implements default zero writeback and execute/writeback bypassing, and compares subsequent results.
tests.expected: All eight registers, including R0, can be written by instructions with data results. Every non-reset edge unconditionally writes the destination and value of W into the registers: arithmetic, logic, shifts, and LOADC use their destination/result; LOAD uses its destination/synchronous read value; other opcodes default to destination R0 and value zero. Thus NOP, STORE, branches, and so on clear R0 when they reach writeback. Execution bypassing likewise provides the default destination R0 and zero value for instructions with no data result; R0 must not be tied to zero, nor may non-writing instructions be assumed to have no register side effects at all.

tests.stimulus: Each of the four ISA software programs and the three added directed software programs places a recognizable result STORE after HALT to detect erroneous continued execution; hold until the next reset, check that there are no subsequent valid and data changes, then reset and restart. Separately check the default firmware's hold after HALT; observe the built-in image as legal software for historical compatibility, without claiming that its tested paths exhaust the entire software domain.
tests.expected: The first four bits 12 indicate HALT. Once X contains HALT, P/I/X/W all hold, and subsequent instructions do not execute; the registers still repeatedly write the held W on every edge. result_valid is computed according to whether a result STORE exists on that edge; HALT itself has no memory transaction, so it becomes zero, while result_data holds. Another synchronous reset can start the program. Verification must be able to observe multiple results produced by the program and their corresponding times; a single result of the default firmware adding four to the input must not be used to represent the entire legal ISA, software domain, or stall behavior.
